correctness.rationale: In a finite space indistinguishable points are closed twins, and the seven specified closed neighborhoods in the antihole are distinct. Thus the induced antihole survives the T0 quotient, and equality in the lower bound forces that quotient to be injective. Minimal open neighborhoods in the stated order convention are principal down-sets; two such neighborhoods intersect precisely when they have a common minimal point. The specified seven points are not minimal, since the closed neighborhood of a minimal point is a clique but the antihole closed neighborhoods are not. A minimal witness serves a clique of induced points. Each edge {j,j+4} has exactly one common antihole neighbor, j+2, and its resulting triangle has no second distance-three edge. Thus seven distinct witnesses are forced. At 14 points they exhaust the remaining points. Comparability of two specified points would nest their induced closed neighborhoods, impossible for distinct closed neighborhoods of size five. Only the optional incidence m_j<x_{j+2} can now be added to the mandatory pair at j. The short edge {i,i+2} occurs precisely when i or i−2 is optional; conversely these conditions generate all desired edges and no forbidden ones. For the count, the complements of the optional sets are independent sets on the step-two cycle. There are one empty set, seven singletons, fourteen pairs at distances two or three in that cycle, and seven triples with gap pattern (2,2,3). These give five dihedral orbits, since the two pair spacings are inequivalent and each other cardinality has one orbit. Order isomorphisms preserve the two levels and must act on the upper level by an antihole automorphism; that determines the witness permutation, so these are the unmarked homeomorphism classes too. The mandatory incidence edges form a spanning 14-cycle, and the optional edges raise the cycle rank to |S|+1. McCord gives precisely the asserted weak equivalences; the four ranks are distinct by first homology.
residual_risks: Applies to induced seven-antiholes at minimum order, not to the full inseparability graph being exactly the antihole, longer antiholes, or ordinary homotopy types of the finite spaces.

value.rationale: The seven-antihole is the smallest odd antihole not isomorphic to an odd hole. Its equality classification makes the finite-space witness correspondence rigid at a natural extremum, and translates an unrestricted topology problem into explicit cycle covers. The result separates five homeomorphism types from four weak types, including two different six-circle cases. This is useful structural information beyond the known minimum cardinality.
residual_risks: No classification for other induced graphs or larger spaces. The contribution is the natural extremal case, not a general odd-antihole theorem.
